Traced src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py. apply_rule_set (l.814-822) parses, builds _Scoping with _choose_prefix, calls _rename_ctes, then _analyze/_rewrite. _choose_prefix (l.365-376) collects lowercased names of every exp.Identifier in the tree (CTE aliases included) plus listed tables and rule tables, and bumps the index until no name starts with sl<k>_. So a model CTE named sl0_* yields prefix sl1_, and no model identifier or table the filters read can start with the guard prefix. _rename_ctes (l.379-402) maps every exp.CTE in the tree (id-keyed from tree.find_all, so an unreferenced CTE such as customer_reps is renamed too) to <prefix>c<n>; every resolved reference is repointed (alias set to the old name when absent so qualifiers like cu.x still resolve), and an unresolvable reference refuses with a name-independent kind. So WITH customer_reps AS (SELECT 1 AS x) SELECT cu.code FROM currencies cu becomes sl0_c0, and the filter body's FROM customer_reps (if a rule read it) resolves to the base table, not the CTE. Later refusals for CTEs (l.298-301, 397) depend on structure and reference shape, not on the name text (the name appears only in the detail string). Whether a statement runs therefore does not depend on a CTE name. Absolute-claim input traced: a CTE named after a table the filter reads, unreferenced, and a CTE starting with sl0_. Caveat: renaming only runs when the set has row rules (l.816), but with no rules no filter reads any table, so the claim's scope is unaffected.

float_literal_text (src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:480-486) returns f"{value:.16e}". For 0.5 this yields '5.0000000000000000e-01' (exact binary value, 16 decimals). For -1e-05 the double is 1.00000000000000008e-05, which rounds at 16 decimals to '-1.0000000000000001e-05'. MySQL's documented numeric literal rules treat a number in scientific notation (digits with e/E exponent) as a floating-point (double) value, and 17 significant digits round-trip a double. Not checked by running code; traced by reading. Non-finite floats are outside the claim's examples.

src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py: _rewrite (583-604) replaces every reference to a row-rule table with _wrap(table, _scoped_body(...)); _scoped_body (405-422) builds SELECT cols FROM t AS guard_alias WHERE <compiled rule> LIMIT 18446744073709551615, a derived table with the visibility filter inside and a LIMIT, which MySQL neither merges into the outer query nor pushes outer conditions into (comment at 179-182). A model expression in a JOIN ON or a select-list scalar subquery only sees the derived table's rows, i.e. visible rows. Hostile inputs traced: (a) model JOIN ON / scalar subquery over orders: the reference is replaced (all base refs are in `base`, no skip path for a rule table; _rewalk 760-763 refuses an unfiltered rule table); (b) a model CTE shadowing a table the filter reads: neutralised by _rename_ctes (379-402) before analysis; (c) a flat [[rls]] table without a row rule: it takes _derived (322-332), not the row-rule path, so the claim (scoped to row-rule tables) is unaffected, and flat RLS only adds predicates inside the guard's derived tables; (d) tampering/mismatch: _proven_scoped_tables (701-733) compares each body's shape to a rebuilt _scoped_body on both the rewritten tree and the re-parsed output (824, 832). The model's expressions never enter the body. The property ultimately depends on MySQL honoring LIMIT as a materialization barrier, which I did not run against a server; the code establishes the construction and refuses any deviation.

src/sqllens/rule_sets.py _Compiler._node (567-636) builds only EQ/NEQ/LT/LTE/GT/GTE (_COMPARISONS 454-456), In, OR/AND (exp.or_/exp.and_), and EXISTS subqueries. No NOT, IS NULL, or COALESCE appears in row-rule compilation (grep of src found exp.Is only in the unrelated catalog filter, safety/rule_sets.py:549, which tests REFERENCED_* IS NULL for information_schema, not a row rule). With != on a NULL status, NULL != 'x' is NULL, not true, so WHERE drops the row. OR of NULLs is NULL (or true only if another branch is true), AND with NULL is never true, so any_of/all_of over NULL never makes a row visible by the NULL itself. The condition is placed directly in WHERE (safety/rule_sets.py:420) with no negation wrapper. Absolute-claim input traced: status != 'closed' with status NULL, and any_of[status != 'a', status != 'b'] with NULL status; both yield NULL, row is filtered out. Caveat: an any_of branch on a different non-NULL true comparison makes the row visible, which is not a NULL comparison making it visible.

_shape (rule_sets.py:425-442) drops only args whose value is None, False, [] (or == those, e.g. int 0) and 'comments'. Operators and structure are Expression nodes, which are kept: NOT is exp.Not, parenthesization is exp.Paren, DISTINCT is exp.Distinct (or Select.distinct arg holding a node); an Expression is never == False/None/[], so none are dropped, and node type names are part of the key. Hostile input traced: Boolean(this=False) vs Boolean(this=True): the False arg is dropped, giving ('Boolean', ()) vs ('Boolean', (('this', True),)), so they still differ; Boolean() with no this generates FALSE as well (same semantics). Literal is_string=False vs True: True is kept, so string vs number literals still differ. Flags like quoted=False/desc=False are dropped only against their absent default, which generates the same SQL. Dropping falsy args also makes parsed trees (which set explicit False flags) comparable with built trees. In _proven_scoped_tables (701-733) the check is _shape(body) != _shape(expected) with expected from _scoped_body, so any extra node (NOT, DISTINCT, Paren, differing literals) changes the key and is refused. Whole check is also backed by prove_compiled_rule (445-450), which compares shapes after generate and reparse. No semantically different body was found that maps to the same shape. I did not run sqlglot; this rests on reading the source only.

In rule_sets.py, _proven_scoped_tables (701-733) skips any rule table whose _wrapper_body is None (719-721), so it is not added to `built`. _rewalk (736-777) then reaches it in traverse_scope sources and, since table.name is in scoping.rules, raises RuleSetRefusal at 760-763 (before the guard-derived/catalog checks could accept it). If it is not a scope source, it is not in `accounted` and line 775-777 refuses it as unaccounted (CTE references use renamed prefixed names).
